'''Numbers''' are abstract mathematical objects used to measure quantity.

== Categories ==

[[File:Types-of-numbers-1-1.svg|500px]]

* '''Natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$''': those used to count discrete objects like bananas or dogs
** e.g., $0,1,2,3\cdots$
* '''Integers $\mathbb{Z}$''': extension of natural numbers to their negative counterparts, used to measure quantities that can be less than 0, like temperature
** e.g., $-10,-5,5,10\cdots$
* '''Rational numbers''' $\mathbb{Q}$: extension of integers to their fractions, used to count discrete objects that can be divided, like $\frac{1}{2}$ cup of a water, $\frac{2}{3}$ of a cucumber pie
** e.g., $2,2.5,-\frac{8847}{8848}\cdots$
<blockquote>
A decimal number like $2.5$ is a rational number if it can be written in fractions of integers. e.g., $2.5=\frac{5}{2}$.
</blockquote>
* '''Real numbers $\mathbb{R}$''': extension of rationals to include decimals that cannot be written as fractions, known as '''irrationals''', like $\pi$

All real numbers can be represented on a '''number axis''':

* '''Complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$''': extension of real numbers to the '''complex plane''' to include '''imaginary numbers''', such as $8i$
** e.g., $8+3i$, $7-5i$

<blockquote>
All imaginary numbers are multiples of $i$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. 

A complex number is the sum of a real number with an imaginary number. It has the general form $a+bi (a,b \in \mathbb{R})$
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
A complex plane is the coordinate plane of a real number axis and an imaginary number axis.

<div class=skin-invert-image>
[[File:Complex-plane.svg|500px]]
</div>
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
Every polynomial of degree $n$ has $n$ roots over the complex number set, i.e.,

$$
\forall a_n,a_{n-1},\ldots,a_0\in\mathbb{C},\ a_n\neq 0,\ \exists z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_n\in\mathbb{C}:\ 
\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k z^k = 0
$$

Which is a direct result of the [[fundamental theorem of algebra#Derived_properties|fundamental theorem of algebra]].
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
In some classifications, real numbers are further classified into '''algebraic numbers $\mathbb{A}$''', which is any real number that is a solution to a homogeneous polynomial equation with ratiaional coefficients. i.e.,

$$
x \in \mathbb{A} \iff \exists a_k \in \mathbb{Q}, \sum_{k=0}^{n \in N*} a_kx^k=0
$$

A non-algebraic real number is known as a '''transcendental''' number.
</blockquote>
